Northwind emailed Marco on Sunday night reporting that their invoices had exported with the wrong tax rate for their Dutch entity, and their finance team only caught it after some had already been sent to clients. [[M1#16]] Diego traced it to the rounding change from August, which only affected accounts with multiple tax jurisdictions — essentially just Northwind. [[M1#17]] Forty-one invoices over two weeks were affected; the calculation fix was quick, but regenerating the already-sent PDFs was the difficult part. [[M1#19]]

Handling:
- Diego fixed the calculation that same day (September 8) and sent a note with the list of affected invoice numbers by the next morning so Northwind could issue corrections. [[M1#20]][[M1#21]]
- Marco called their CFO himself and told Diego not to promise any compensation in the note; the credit decision would come after the call. [[M1#20]][[M1#23]]
- By the September 15 sync it was closed: corrected invoices went out, Northwind's finance team confirmed the numbers, and the CFO replied to Marco's note. [[M2#9]] Marco decided to give them one month free and Ana applied the credit that day. [[M2#10]][[M2#11]]

At the retro, Diego listed Northwind as something that went well — a bad week, fixed in a day, and the customer stayed. [[M4#2]]

No. The decision was made in the September 1 Q4 planning meeting: no mobile app in Q4, revisit in January if the mobile session share changes. [[M1#25]] The reasoning was that only about eight percent of sessions are on a phone, and most of those are people checking invoice status, which the responsive site already handles [[M1#23]], and building it would consume the whole quarter for two people [[M1#24]].

Marco reaffirmed it on September 8: the mobile app is not happening, January at the earliest, and Q4 order is pricing, then checkout, then SOC 2 groundwork, with nothing added unless something is removed. [[M4#25]] At the September 29 retro he said cutting it was deliberate and he had zero regrets, since the people asking want a feature the responsive site already has. [[M2#23]]

Two related follow-ups: Sofía was to add a note to the support macro so the team stops promising it [[M1#26]], and note that the AI note-taker's summary wrongly claimed the team decided to build the mobile app — the opposite of the actual decision, which was part of why the trial was cancelled. [[M1#22]] Marco also noted the process started late because he sat on the quotes for a month, and said he will no longer own procurement. [[M1#23]]
